Reliance Q2 FY27 Results: Why Shares Rallied Over 6% After Record Earnings
sum: Reliance Industries shares rallied more than 6% in early trading on November 2, 2026, after the company announced strong September-quarter earnings. The stock’s reaction reflected investor enthusiasm about record group earnings, led by its oil-to-chemicals business. The gain was an intraday move, rather than a closing-session return.

However, the Reliance Q2 FY27 results tell a more detailed story than the headline rally suggests. Energy earnings surged, digital services continued growing, and retail profitability remained under pressure. Understanding these differences is part of fundamental analysis of Indian stocks.
For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Reliance reported the following consolidated figures:
These figures use the company’s stated reporting definitions. Gross revenue and different profit measures should not be treated as interchangeable.

EBITDA stands for earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. It helps assess operating earnings before these expenses, but it does not show how much cash remains after capital expenditure and other payments.

The ₹29,550 crore profit figure includes Reliance’s share of earnings from associates and joint ventures. It should be described with that qualification rather than presented as profit attributable solely to Reliance shareholders.
The quarter combined a sharp improvement in energy earnings with continued growth in digital services.

sum: - Reliance Industries' Q2 FY27 net profit rose 41% year on year to ₹25,548 crore.
- Reliance Industries' revenue increased 29% year on year to ₹3.32 lakh crore.
- Supreme Industries reported 24% Plastic Piping System volume growth in Q2 FY27.

Q2 FY27 results had been declared by 1,803 companies as of November 4, 2026, covering the July-September 2026 quarter, while Reliance Industries reported a 41% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹25,548 crore. The earnings calendar has brought updates across banking, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, power, consumer businesses and industrial companies.

A total of 1,803 companies had declared their Q2 FY27 results by November 4, 2026. FY27 refers to the financial year ending March 2027, and the second quarter covers the July-September 2026 period. The announced results therefore provide an update on corporate performance during the September quarter.

The calendar included large-cap companies and other closely tracked listed businesses. Results announced on November 4 included BSE, Cummins India, Zydus Lifesciences, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise, Lenskart Solutions, Power Finance Corporation, FSN E-Commerce Ventures, Aurobindo Pharma, NHPC, Dabur India, Torrent Power, Biocon, Balkrishna Industries, Premier Energies, PI Industries and Physicswallah.

The reporting schedule also featured companies such as State Bank of India, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Holdings & Investment, Lupin and AIA on November 3. The range of companies reporting during the period spans financial services, pharmaceuticals, electricity, consumer products, engineering and new-age businesses.

sum: New Delhi, Nov. 4 -- Reliance Industries share price will remain in focus on Wednesday after Mukesh Ambani-led stock emerged as the stock with the highest exposure in the Margin Trading Facility (MTF) book after recording their biggest single-day rally in six years on Monday, November 2,

According to the latest data released by the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on November 2, Reliance Industries' MTF exposure jumped 60% to Rs.4,711 crore, compared with Rs.2,937 crore recorded at the end of October 30.
With this sharp increase, Reliance Industries has overtaken HDFC Bank to claim the top position in the MTF book, which the private lender had held for several months.

The overall MTF book stood at Rs.1.45 lakh crore, with the top 10 stocks accounting for an exposure of Rs.19,442 crore. Following Monday's surge, Reliance Industries alone accounted for 24% of the total exposure among these top 10 stocks.

Reliance Industries also continued to be the most traded stock in the Nifty 500 index on both Monday and Tuesday. Its trading turnover exceeded Rs.11,000 crore on Monday and remained above Rs.5,000 crore on Tuesday. Tuesday's session also witnessed delivery-based buying worth nearly Rs.3,000 crore, following purchases of more than Rs.6,000 crore in delivery volumes on Monday.
On November 2, Reliance Industries share price surged nearly 11.6% in a single session, accompanied by an extraordinary volume breakout.

"The stock has decisively broken above a prolonged downward sloping trendline, suggesting that selling pressure may finally be giving way to fresh buying interest. The confluence of a technical breakout, exceptional volumes, improving earnings and value unlocking through Jio makes Reliance an interesting stock to watch," said Apurva Sheth, Head of Market Perspectives and Research, SAMCO Securities.

sum: New Delhi, Nov. 3 -- Reliance Industries share price: Reliance Industries share price declined over 1% in intraday trade on Tuesday, November 3, on profit booking after rallying nearly 12% in the previous session. The stock fell as much as 1.3% to an intraday low of Rs.1,281.55 on the NSE, giving back some of Monday's sharp gains.

Reliance Industries shares had surged 11.6% on Monday to close at Rs.1,300, their highest level since early September. The rally marked the stock's biggest single-day gain since April 2020 and helped lift the Nifty 50 by 1.7%, given the company's heavyweight presence in the index.

The sharp rebound also added Rs.1.84 lakh crore to Reliance Industries' market capitalisation, taking it to Rs.17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India's most valuable listed company. At its peak of Rs.1,611, the company had commanded a market capitalisation of Rs.21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the Rs.21 lakh crore milestone in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve the feat.

Despite Monday's rally, Reliance shares remain down 17.22% so far in 2026. The stock had been under pressure for much of the year, closing lower in eight of the previous 10 months. The latest gains followed the company's record quarterly profit, which renewed investor interest in the stock.

Reliance Industries reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs.29,550 crore for Q2FY27, marking a 33.8% increase from Rs.22,092 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs.3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record Rs.62,409 crore.

The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business was the biggest contributor to the strong performance. Its EBITDA surged 67.9% to Rs.25,203 crore, supported by higher global fuel margins and improved petrochemical spreads. O2C revenue increased 44.2% to Rs.2,31,601 crore, with supply disruptions in West Asia and other regions pushing transportation fuel cracks higher.

Digital services also supported earnings, while retail remained a relative weak spot. Reliance Retail Ventures reported a 24.3% decline in PAT to Rs.2,611 crore, despite a 6.4% rise in revenue to Rs.91,716 crore. Its EBITDA, before a one-time impairment charge, fell 8.6% to Rs.6,228 crore.

sum: New Delhi, Nov. 2 -- Reliance Industries share price surged as much as 5.91% in Monday's trading session after the Mukesh Ambani-led oil-to-telecom conglomerate reported strong set of numbers during the July-September quarter FY27.
RIL stock opened at Rs.1,228.10 apiece on NSE today, as compared to previous close of Rs.1,164.90 last week on Friday and touched an intraday high of Rs.1,237.30 on 2 November.

Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) reported a 33.8% year-on-year (YoY) growth in consolidated profit after tax (PAT), including its share of associates and joint ventures, at Rs.29,550 crore for Q2FY27, compared with Rs.22,092 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Net profit attributable to the company's shareholders increased 40% YoY to Rs.25,548 crore.

The company's consolidated revenue rose 27.8% YoY to Rs.3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record Rs.62,409 crore. The latest quarterly profit also surpassed the Rs.23,196 crore recorded in the previous quarter, marking a fresh high for India's largest listed company by market capitalisation.

The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) segment was the biggest contributor to earnings growth, supported by stronger global transportation fuel cracks and an improvement in petrochemical margins. The segment's EBITDA surged 67.9% YoY to Rs.25,203 crore, while revenue climbed 44.2% to Rs.2,31,601 crore.

Global supply disruptions arising from the West Asia conflict, including tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, as well as attacks on refining infrastructure across the region and Russia, drove fuel cracks to 3-3.7 times their year-ago levels. Meanwhile, the average price of Dated Brent crude stood at $97 per barrel during the quarter, registering a 40.6% YoY increase.

The improvement in refining margins came despite geopolitical uncertainties, higher crude premiums and elevated freight costs. Reliance said its diversified crude procurement strategy and flexibility in optimising product placement helped it capitalise on favourable market conditions. The company also achieved its highest-ever crude processing volumes by increasing supplies from the Americas and the Mediterranean and redirecting exports towards markets offering better net realisations.

sum: New Delhi, Nov. 1 -- Reliance Industries shares are likely to remain in focus on Monday, 2 November, after the Mukesh Ambani-led conglomerate reported a record quarterly profit for the July-September quarter on Friday, 30 October. The company's strong performance was driven by a sharp recovery in its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business and continued growth in digital services, which helped offset relatively subdued earnings from retail.

Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) reported a consolidated profit after tax, including its share of associates and joint ventures, of Rs.29,550 crore in the second quarter of FY27, marking a 33.8% increase from Rs.22,092 crore in the corresponding period last year. Net profit attributable to owners of the company rose 40% year-on-year to Rs.25,548 crore.

Consolidated revenue increased 27.8% year-on-year to Rs.3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA grew 23.9% to a record Rs.62,409 crore. The latest quarterly profit also exceeded the Rs.23,196 crore reported in the previous quarter, setting a new high for India's largest listed company by market capitalisation.

The O2C business emerged as the biggest contributor to earnings growth, benefiting from stronger global transportation fuel cracks and improving petrochemical margins. EBITDA from the segment jumped 67.9% year-on-year to Rs.25,203 crore, while revenue rose 44.2% to Rs.2,31,601 crore.

Global supply disruptions linked to the West Asia conflict, including tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, along with attacks on refining infrastructure in the region and Russia, pushed fuel cracks to 3.0-3.7 times their year-ago levels. Dated Brent crude averaged $97 per barrel during the quarter, up 40.6% year-on-year.

The improvement in refining margins came despite challenges from geopolitical disruptions, higher crude premiums and rising freight costs. Reliance said its diversified crude sourcing strategy and ability to optimise product placement helped it capture stronger margins. The company recorded its highest-ever crude processing volumes by increasing supplies from the Americas and the Mediterranean and by redirecting exports to markets offering better net realisations.

sum: NEW DELHI: Jio Platforms Limited, Reliance Industries’ digital and telecom arm, made a strong stock market debut on Wednesday, October 28, with its shares opening at a 21.36 per cent premium to the IPO issue price. The listing propelled the company to a market valuation of approximately Rs 12.5 lakh crore, making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after its parent, Reliance Industries.

The shares opened at Rs 1,358 apiece on both the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE), against the issue price of Rs 1,119. The strong debut followed India’s largest initial public offering, valued at approximately Rs 30,213 crore, which witnessed overwhelming demand from institutional and retail investors.

The stock subsequently extended its gains and closed its first trading session at Rs 1,419, approximately 26.81 per cent above the IPO price. The Jio Platforms IPO marked a major return to the primary market for the Reliance Group, approximately two decades after Reliance Petroleum’s public offering in 2006.

The listing marks a significant milestone for the Reliance Group, strengthening its dominance in India’s corporate landscape and highlighting investor confidence in the country’s rapidly expanding digital economy. It also represented another milestone in the group’s expansion beyond its traditional energy and petrochemicals businesses.
The issue attracted more than one crore investor applications, reflecting widespread participation. The supplied report puts the figure at 1.34 crore, although published estimates vary.
Jio Platforms raised approximately Rs 30,213 crore through its public offering, surpassing Hyundai Motor India’s Rs 27,870-crore IPO and LIC’s Rs 21,008-crore issue.
The offering became a landmark event in India’s primary equity market.

Jio Platforms IPO: Shares Jump 21% on Listing After Record ₹30,213 Crore Offering
sum: Jio Platforms, the digital and telecom business of Reliance Industries, has made a historic stock market debut on October 28, 2026, with its shares opening at a 21.36 percent premium following India’s largest initial public offering (IPO) of ₹30,213 crore.

Jio Platforms shares opened at ₹1,358 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), compared with the IPO issue price of ₹1,119. The ₹239 increase per share reflected strong investor demand for India’s largest telecom operator and its expanding digital services business.

The listing valued Jio Platforms at approximately ₹12.5 lakh crore, making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries. Jio also overtook Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank in market capitalization.
The IPO marked Reliance Industries’ first major stock market listing in two decades and delivered the strongest debut premium among India’s five largest IPOs by issue size.
Jio Platforms’ ₹30,213 crore IPO attracted bids worth more than ₹7.4 lakh crore, demonstrating substantial investor interest in India’s telecommunications and digital infrastructure market.
The IPO received approximately 1.39 crore applications, setting a new participation benchmark for India’s primary market.
Ahead of the public offering, Jio Platforms raised approximately ₹8,110 crore from 212 anchor investors.

sum: Stock market rally: The Sensex and Nifty 50 surged over 2% during intraday trade, raising hopes of a sustained recovery on Dalal Street ahead of Diwali. The rally came amid improving corporate earnings, renewed interest in large-cap stocks and a sharp correction in artificial intelligence-linked equities overseas.

The 30-share Sensex jumped more than 1,500 points, or over 2%, to touch an intraday high of 74,330. Meanwhile, the Nifty 50 climbed approximately 433 points, or 1.9%, to hit the day's high of 23,056, reclaiming the psychologically important 23,000 mark.
Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments Limited, attributed the domestic market's strength to better technology earnings, currency stability and easing bond yields.

"Indian equities advanced as stronger-than-expected technology earnings boosted confidence in corporate profit growth and lifted benchmark-heavy large-cap stocks. Rupee stability and easing bond yields further supported sentiment, bringing financial stocks into focus," Nair said. Nair believes that the strong IT-led earnings season and expectations of decent overall Q2 corporate performance indicated resilience despite a challenging global environment.
IT stocks emerged as key drivers of Thursday's market rally, with Tata Consultancy ServicesHCL TechnologiesTech Mahindra

The rally came even as Asian markets tumbled amid concerns over elevated valuations of artificial intelligence-linked stocks. US consumer inflation rose faster than expected, raising questions about the Federal Reserve's policy outlook. The correction in AI stocks could benefit Indian equities, which have underperformed markets riding the global AI boom.
V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, said the correction could change foreign investor flows.

sum: On Wednesday late evening, details emerged that Jio Platforms Ltd, the digital and telecom arm of Reliance Industries, has set a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 per share for its initial public offering (IPO) that could raise about ₹30,213 crore at the top of the range, making it India's largest.
The stock jumped as much as 2.56% to ₹1204.7 on the NSE. Image: Shutterstock
Shares of Reliance Industries (RIL), the oil-to-telecom conglomerate, rallied over 2% in the morning trade on Thursday, October 15, following the unveiling of Reliance Jio's much-awaited IPO details.

The IPO committee of Jio Platforms' board approved the band at a meeting on Wednesday, the filing said. Eligible employees bidding in the employee reservation portion will get a discount of ₹54 per share.
Investors must bid for at least 12 shares and in multiples of 12 thereafter. At the cap price, one lot would cost ₹13,428.

According to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), the company plans to issue up to 27 crore equity shares with a face value of ₹10 each. At the cap price, that works out to ₹30,213 crore, by calculation. That is about 8% above the record set by Hyundai Motor India, whose ₹27,858.75 crore IPO in 2024 holds the top spot.
The Jio IPO could help unlock value for Reliance Industries (RIL) by giving investors a clearer idea of how much its telecom business is worth as a standalone company.

Let’s examine the latest developments and what they could mean for investors.
As of 2:20 PM, Reliance Industries was trading firmly in positive territory.
The sharp rise indicates that investors welcomed the latest business developments and expect them to strengthen Reliance’s long-term growth prospects.

One of the biggest catalysts for the stock was a reported announcement by US President Donald Trump regarding a proposed US$300 billion partnership involving Reliance Industries to develop a major refinery project in Texas.
If the project progresses, it could represent one of the most significant international expansions in the company’s history.
